title: Functionality and Data Stealing by Pseudo-Client Attack and Target Defenses in Split Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
motivation: Semi-honest server in split learning can steal client functionality without knowing client model structure; prior attacks fail on complex models.
problem_framing: Design attack for semi-honest server to steal functionality, reconstruct inputs, infer labels without client model knowledge.
key_insight: Well-trained server model alone provides enough info to train pseudo-client model with very limited samples; intermediate server models during SL guide better pseudo-client convergence.
method_signature: PCAT: Pseudo-Client Attack trains fake client model using server model as constraint while SL runs normally.
evaluation_criteria: Attack accuracy vs baseline accuracy; functionality gap; input reconstruction quality (SSIM); label inference accuracy.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Adding Gaussian noise does NOT prevent PCAT but enhances functionality stealing ability (unexpected). Their proposed defense 'will fail' under improved PCAT in U-shape SL.
evidence_for_taste: the attack is transparent to clients
the solution space could be too large
without any preknowledge about the client model
breaking the similarity between their input-label pairs
thinking_moves: 把攻击从model inversion重新frame成knowledge distillation问题
利用server model自身的知识而非smashed data来构造伪客户端
先提出防御机制再设计绕过方案,形成对抗性迭代
从单层模型攻击扩展到复杂深度网络,验证方法通用性
意外发现噪声反而增强攻击效果,提示防御不能只看数据扰动
